svg.title: rocketmq-namesrv architecture
svg.desc: The NameServer binary merges its configuration file and command line, validates a security bootstrap profile, and hands a service context, telemetry, the server and client configuration and the transport security to the Builder. NameServerBootstrap initializes and starts the runtime, whose state moves from Created through Initialized and Running to ShuttingDown and Stopped. Brokers, clients and admin tools reach the remoting server. The request dispatcher tracks requests in flight, classifies each request as route read, broker control, admin read or admin write, applies layered authorization and workload admission, and routes by request code. ClientRequestProcessor answers topic route lookups, ClusterTestRequestProcessor takes its place in cluster-test mode, and DefaultRequestProcessor handles every other request code. In the route manager, one mutation gate serializes every change to six source tables for topic queues, broker addresses, clusters, live brokers, filter servers and queue mappings, and each change publishes immutable per-topic route snapshots, which route lookups load without the gate. Broker liveness reacts to closed sessions, scans for expired brokers and unregisters them in batches. The config stores persist KV configuration and runtime configuration through the metadata I/O actor before making them visible. An outbound client, a cluster-test lookup and an embedded controller are optional. ServiceLifecycle provides probes and the shutdown deadline, and telemetry is exported when configured. Two rows list the order in which start-up brings the parts up and shutdown takes them down. Where motion is allowed, a looping tour plays six steps: boot, register, route lookup, expire, admin and shut down.
svg.text: Service discovery and routing for brokers, clients and admin tools.

g.text: batches run under the mutation gate
